subproblem.title: Integer median of an integer-valued function on the unit cube (Simon 6.5.1 (31), (35); parent steps 1–2)
subproblem.statement: Let m ∈ ℕ, n := m + 1, Q₁ := {y ∈ ℝⁿ : 0 < y_i < 1 for all i} ⊆ Euclid (m + 1) and Lⁿ := volume. Let u : ℝⁿ → ℝ take an integer value at every point (u(y) ∈ ℤ for all y) and be integrable on Q₁. Then there is β ∈ ℤ such that Lⁿ(Q₁ ∩ {y : β ≤ u(y)}) ≥ 1/2 and Lⁿ(Q₁ ∩ {y : u(y) ≤ β}) ≥ 1/2 (measures in [0, ∞]) and |β| ≤ 2∫_{Q₁}|u|.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (m : ℕ) (u : Euclid (m + 1) → ℝ), (∀ y, ∃ z : ℤ, u y = z) → IntegrableOn u {y : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1} → ∃ β : ℤ, 1 / 2 ≤ volume ({y : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1} ∩ {y | (β : ℝ) ≤ u y}) ∧ 1 / 2 ≤ volume ({y : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1} ∩ {y | u y ≤ (β : ℝ)}) ∧ |(β : ℝ)| ≤ 2 * ∫ y in {y : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1}, |u y|
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, steps 1 and 2, i.e. the choice (31) of the integer β_F and the bound (35) in Simon's proof of the Deformation Theorem (Ch. 6, 5.1; chapter-06.txt). Notation: n := m + 1, Q₁ := {y : 0 < y_i < 1 for all i}, Lⁿ := volume on Euclid n, μ := Lⁿ⌞Q₁ (volume.restrict Q₁).

0. Preliminaries.
 (a) Q₁ is open (a finite intersection of the open sets {y : 0 < y_i} and {y : y_i < 1}; the coordinate maps y ↦ y_i are continuous), hence Borel.
 (b) Lⁿ(Q₁) = 1. The coordinate map y ↦ (y_0, …, y_m) (WithLp.ofLp) is a measure-preserving bijection from Euclid n onto ℝ^{Fin n} with the product Lebesgue measure (PiLp.volume_preserving_ofLp; inverse PiLp.volume_preserving_toLp). It maps Q₁ onto the box ∏_i (0, 1) = Set.pi univ (fun _ => Ioo 0 1), whose measure is ∏_i (1 − 0) = 1 (Real.volume_pi_Ioo).
 (c) Measurable representative. u is integrable on Q₁, so it is a.e.-strongly measurable for μ. Fix a Borel function ũ with u = ũ μ-almost everywhere. The set Z := Q₁ ∩ {u ≠ ũ} is Lⁿ-null (Q₁ is measurable, so μ-null subsets of Q₁ are Lⁿ-null). Hence for every Borel set B ⊆ ℝ the sets Q₁ ∩ u⁻¹(B) and Q₁ ∩ ũ⁻¹(B) differ only inside Z. So Q₁ ∩ u⁻¹(B) is Lⁿ-null-measurable and has the same Lⁿ-measure as the Borel set Q₁ ∩ ũ⁻¹(B). This applies in particular to A_b := Q₁ ∩ {u ≤ b} and to Q₁ ∩ {b ≤ u}, for b ∈ ℝ.

1. The distribution function. For b ∈ ℤ put F(b) := Lⁿ(A_b) ∈ [0, 1]. F is nondecreasing, since A_b ⊆ A_{b'} for b ≤ b'.
 – F(N) → 1 as N → ∞ (N ∈ ℕ). Indeed, the sets A_N increase, and their union is Q₁ because u is real-valued. Continuity of measure from below (tendsto_measure_iUnion_atTop) gives F(N) → Lⁿ(Q₁) = 1. Since 1/2 < 1, there is N₁ ∈ ℕ with F(N₁) > 1/2.
 – F(−N) → 0 as N → ∞. The sets A_{−N} decrease, are null-measurable, have finite measure (≤ 1), and have empty intersection. Continuity from above (tendsto_measure_iInter_atTop) gives F(−N) → 0. Hence there is N₀ ∈ ℕ with F(−N₀) < 1/2. By monotonicity, F(b) < 1/2 for every integer b ≤ −N₀.

2. Choice of β (Simon (31)). The set S := {b ∈ ℤ : F(b) ≥ 1/2} contains N₁. Every element of S is > −N₀, so S is bounded below. Let β be its least element (Int.exists_least_of_bdd, or csInf_mem in ℤ). Then F(β) ≥ 1/2 and, as β − 1 ∉ S, F(β − 1) < 1/2.

3. Two-sided median property.
 – First, Lⁿ(Q₁ ∩ {u ≤ β}) = F(β) ≥ 1/2.
 – Second, u is integer-valued. So for every y, β ≤ u(y) holds iff u(y) ≤ β − 1 fails: if u(y) = z ∈ ℤ, then β ≤ z ⟺ ¬(z ≤ β − 1). Hence Q₁ ∩ {β ≤ u} = Q₁ ∖ A_{β−1}. The set A_{β−1} ⊆ Q₁ is null-measurable with finite measure, so (measure_diff) Lⁿ(Q₁ ∩ {β ≤ u}) = Lⁿ(Q₁) − F(β − 1) = 1 − F(β − 1) > 1/2 ≥ 1/2.

4. The bound |β| ≤ 2∫_{Q₁}|u| (Simon (35)). Both functions below are integrable on Q₁.
 – β = 0. The claim is 0 ≤ 2∫_{Q₁}|u|, which is true.
 – β > 0. For μ-a.e. y (namely y ∈ Q₁ ∖ Z) we have |u(y)| ≥ β·1_{β ≤ ũ}(y). Indeed, if β ≤ ũ(y) = u(y) then |u(y)| ≥ u(y) ≥ β, and otherwise |u(y)| ≥ 0. Integrating over Q₁ gives ∫_{Q₁}|u| ≥ β·Lⁿ(Q₁ ∩ {β ≤ ũ}) = β·Lⁿ(Q₁ ∩ {β ≤ u}) ≥ β/2, by 0(c) and step 3.
 – β < 0. Likewise |u(y)| ≥ −u(y) ≥ −β = |β| on Q₁ ∩ {u ≤ β}. So ∫_{Q₁}|u| ≥ |β|·Lⁿ(Q₁ ∩ {u ≤ β}) ≥ |β|/2.
In every case |β| ≤ 2∫_{Q₁}|u|.

Steps 3 and 4 give the three conclusions for this β. ∎
proof_key_steps: Lⁿ(Q₁) = 1 via the measure-preserving coordinate map; a Borel representative ũ makes the level sets of u null-measurable with the same measures.
F(b) = Lⁿ(Q₁ ∩ {u ≤ b}) is nondecreasing with F → 1 at +∞ and F → 0 at −∞ (continuity of measure).
β := least integer with F(β) ≥ 1/2; integrality gives Q₁ ∩ {β ≤ u} = Q₁ ∖ {u ≤ β − 1}, of measure 1 − F(β − 1) > 1/2.
Integrating |u| ≥ |β| over the half-measure set {β ≤ u} (β > 0) or {u ≤ β} (β < 0) gives |β| ≤ 2∫_{Q₁}|u|.

audit.reason: The type matches all stated hypotheses. Measurable representatives justify the level-set measures; continuity of measure gives a least integer crossing 1/2. Integrality supplies the opposite half-measure set, and the three sign cases prove the required bound on beta without circular reliance.

subproblem.title: Deviation from a θ-median is controlled by the double-integral oscillation (Simon Ch. 2, 2.7; parent step 3)
subproblem.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, W ⊆ Euclid P measurable with L(W) := volume(W) < ∞, v : Euclid P → ℝ integrable on W, β ∈ ℝ and θ > 0 with θ·L(W) ≤ L(W ∩ {β ≤ v}) and θ·L(W) ≤ L(W ∩ {v ≤ β}) (real numbers via toReal). Then ∫_W |v − β| ≤ (1 + θ⁻¹)·L(W)⁻¹·∫_W ∫_W |v(x) − v(y)| dy dx, where 0⁻¹ := 0.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (W : Set (Euclid P)) (v : Euclid P → ℝ) (β θ : ℝ), MeasurableSet W → volume W ≠ ∞ → IntegrableOn v W → 0 < θ → θ * (volume W).toReal ≤ (volume (W ∩ {y | β ≤ v y})).toReal → θ * (volume W).toReal ≤ (volume (W ∩ {y | v y ≤ β})).toReal → ∫ y in W, |v y - β| ≤ (1 + θ⁻¹) * ((volume W).toReal)⁻¹ * ∫ x in W, ∫ y in W, |v x - v y|
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, step 3. Its first line is ∫_Q|v − v̄| ≤ Lⁿ(Q)⁻¹∫_Q∫_Q|v(x) − v(y)|. Its 'Consequently' paragraph replaces the mean v̄ by a θ-median β' with factor 1 + θ⁻¹ (Simon Ch. 2, Lemma 2.7, condition (∗)). Both hold for any integrable v; this child is the combination of the two. Notation: |W| := volume(W).toReal ∈ [0, ∞), and all integrals are over subsets of W.

0. Degenerate case. If |W| = 0, then volume(W) = 0 (it is finite), so the restricted measure volume⌞W is zero and every integral over W vanishes. Both sides are then 0; the right side has the factor ∫_W(…) = 0. Assume |W| > 0 from now on, and put v̄ := |W|⁻¹∫_W v.

1. Integrability.
 – For each fixed x, y ↦ |v(x) − v(y)| is integrable on W: it is a.e.-strongly measurable and bounded by |v(x)| + |v(y)|, and constants are integrable on W because volume(W) < ∞.
 – The function (x, y) ↦ |v(x) − v(y)| is integrable on W × W for (volume⌞W) ⊗ (volume⌞W). It is a.e.-strongly measurable (compose v with the two projections: AEStronglyMeasurable.fst/snd) and bounded by |v(x)| + |v(y)|, which is integrable for the finite product measure.
 – Hence (Fubini, Integrable.integral_prod_left) the function x ↦ ∫_W|v(x) − v(y)| dy is integrable on W.
 – Likewise x ↦ |v(x) − v̄| and x ↦ |v(x) − β| are integrable on W.

2. Mean step (the Jensen step of parent step 3). For x ∈ W, linearity of the integral gives v(x) − v̄ = |W|⁻¹∫_W (v(x) − v(y)) dy. Hence |v(x) − v̄| ≤ |W|⁻¹∫_W|v(x) − v(y)| dy. Integrate over W and use step 1 (integral_mono):
 (∗) ∫_W|v − v̄| ≤ |W|⁻¹∫_W∫_W|v(x) − v(y)| dy dx.

3. Median replacement (parent step 3, 'Consequently'). Let ṽ be a Borel function with v = ṽ a.e. on W. The sets W ∩ {β ≤ v} and W ∩ {β ≤ ṽ} differ by a null set, so they have the same measure; the same holds for W ∩ {v ≤ β} and W ∩ {ṽ ≤ β}.
 – Case β ≥ v̄. On the measurable set E₊ := W ∩ {β ≤ ṽ} we have, a.e., |v − v̄| ≥ v − v̄ ≥ β − v̄ ≥ 0. Hence (β − v̄)·volume(E₊).toReal ≤ ∫_{E₊}|v − v̄| ≤ ∫_W|v − v̄|. Here volume(E₊).toReal = volume(W ∩ {β ≤ v}).toReal ≥ θ|W| by hypothesis, and β − v̄ ≥ 0. So (β − v̄)θ|W| ≤ ∫_W|v − v̄|, i.e. |β − v̄|·|W| ≤ θ⁻¹∫_W|v − v̄|.
 – Case β < v̄. Use E₋ := W ∩ {ṽ ≤ β}: there |v − v̄| ≥ v̄ − v ≥ v̄ − β > 0 a.e. With the second hypothesis this gives the same inequality |β − v̄|·|W| ≤ θ⁻¹∫_W|v − v̄|.

4. Conclusion. Pointwise |v − β| ≤ |v − v̄| + |v̄ − β|. Integrating over W:
 ∫_W|v − β| ≤ ∫_W|v − v̄| + |v̄ − β|·|W|
  ≤ (1 + θ⁻¹)∫_W|v − v̄| (step 3)
  ≤ (1 + θ⁻¹)·|W|⁻¹·∫_W∫_W|v(x) − v(y)| dy dx (step 2, (∗)). ∎
proof_key_steps: If volume(W) = 0 both sides vanish; otherwise put v̄ := |W|⁻¹∫_W v and check integrability of all integrands (Fubini for the partial integral).
Jensen step: |v(x) − v̄| ≤ |W|⁻¹∫_W|v(x) − v(y)|dy, integrated over W.
θ-median step: on {β ≤ v} (if β ≥ v̄) or {v ≤ β} (if β < v̄) one has |v − v̄| ≥ |β − v̄|, so |β − v̄||W| ≤ θ⁻¹∫_W|v − v̄|.
Triangle inequality: ∫_W|v − β| ≤ (1 + θ⁻¹)∫_W|v − v̄| ≤ (1 + θ⁻¹)|W|⁻¹∫∫|v(x) − v(y)|.

audit.reason: The proof handles zero measure explicitly and establishes product integrability before using Fubini. The mean estimate and the two median inequalities give exactly the stated factor 1 + theta⁻¹. No additional theta ≤ 1 hypothesis is needed.

subproblem.title: Fubini identity for mixed points on the cube Q_δ (the Fubini step of parent step 3)
subproblem.statement: Let m ∈ ℕ, δ ∈ ℝ, k ∈ Fin (m + 1), Q_δ := {y ∈ Euclid (m + 1) : δ < y_i < 1 − δ for all i}, and let h : Euclid (m + 1) → ℝ be integrable on Q_δ. For x, y let a_k(x, y) be the point whose j-th coordinate is y_j for j < k and x_j for j ≥ k. Then ∫_{Q_δ} ∫_{Q_δ} h(a_k(x, y)) dy dx = volume(Q_δ)·∫_{Q_δ} h.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (m : ℕ) (δ : ℝ) (k : Fin (m + 1)) (h : Euclid (m + 1) → ℝ), IntegrableOn h {y : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, δ < y i ∧ y i < 1 - δ} → ∫ x in {y : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, δ < y i ∧ y i < 1 - δ}, ∫ y in {y : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, δ < y i ∧ y i < 1 - δ}, h (WithLp.toLp 2 (fun j => if j < k then y j else x j)) = (volume {y : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, δ < y i ∧ y i < 1 - δ}).toReal * ∫ x in {y : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, δ < y i ∧ y i < 1 - δ}, h x
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, step 3: 'Integrating over x, y ∈ Q (Fubini) bounds the i-th term'. The integrand h(a_k(x, y)) does not involve the variables x_j (j < k) or y_j (j ≥ k). Integrating them out gives the factor volume(Q_δ). This is that Fubini step, made precise by a coordinate swap. Notation: E := Euclid (m + 1), n := m + 1, μ := volume on E, Q := Q_δ.

1. The swap σ. Define σ : E × E → E × E by σ(x, y) := (a_k(x, y), c_k(x, y)), where c_k(x, y) has j-th coordinate x_j for j < k and y_j for j ≥ k. Thus σ exchanges the j-th coordinates of x and y for every j < k and fixes all other coordinates. Clearly σ(σ(p)) = p for all p. So σ is a bijection that is its own inverse, and (being measurable, step 2) a measurable equivalence; in particular it is a measurable embedding.

2. σ preserves μ ⊗ μ.
 – The coordinate map WithLp.ofLp : E → ℝ^{Fin n} preserves volume (PiLp.volume_preserving_ofLp), and so does its inverse WithLp.toLp (PiLp.volume_preserving_toLp). Taking products (MeasurePreserving.prod), it suffices to show that τ(x, y) := ((j ↦ y_j if j < k else x_j), (j ↦ x_j if j < k else y_j)) preserves volume ⊗ volume on (ℝ^{Fin n})².
 – Identify (ℝ^{Fin n})² with (ℝ × ℝ)^{Fin n}: the identification (MeasurableEquiv.arrowProdEquivProdArrow) maps the product measure ∏_j (L¹ ⊗ L¹) to (∏_j L¹) ⊗ (∏_j L¹) (measurePreserving_arrowProdEquivProdArrow).
 – In these coordinates τ acts factorwise: by the swap (s, t) ↦ (t, s) on the j-th factor ℝ × ℝ when j < k, and by the identity when j ≥ k. Each factor map preserves L¹ ⊗ L¹ (Measure.measurePreserving_swap; MeasurePreserving.id). So the factorwise map preserves the product measure (measurePreserving_pi).
 – Composing these measure-preserving maps shows that τ, and hence σ, is measure preserving.

3. σ⁻¹(Q × Q) = Q × Q. Q is the product of the same interval (δ, 1 − δ) in every coordinate. σ only exchanges coordinates between the two factors, so σ(x, y) ∈ Q × Q iff every coordinate of x and of y lies in (δ, 1 − δ), i.e. iff (x, y) ∈ Q × Q. Consequently σ preserves the restricted measure (μ ⊗ μ)⌞(Q × Q) (MeasurePreserving.restrict_preimage_emb). This measure equals (μ⌞Q) ⊗ (μ⌞Q) (Measure.prod_restrict).

4. Integrability.
 – Q is bounded (|y_i| ≤ |δ| + |1 − δ| for every coordinate), so volume(Q) < ∞ and μ⌞Q is a finite measure.
 – Since h is integrable for μ⌞Q, the function (x, y) ↦ h(x) is integrable for (μ⌞Q) ⊗ (μ⌞Q) (Integrable.comp_fst).
 – Since σ preserves this measure and is a measurable embedding (MeasurePreserving.integrable_comp_emb), (x, y) ↦ h(σ(x, y)₁) = h(a_k(x, y)) is integrable as well.

5. Computation.
 ∫_Q ∫_Q h(a_k(x, y)) dy dx
  = ∫_{Q×Q} h(σ(x, y)₁) d((μ⌞Q) ⊗ (μ⌞Q)) (Fubini, integral_prod, step 4)
  = ∫_{Q×Q} h(x) d((μ⌞Q) ⊗ (μ⌞Q))(x, y) (measure preservation, MeasurePreserving.integral_comp, step 3)
  = ∫_Q (∫_Q 1 dy) h(x) dx (Fubini, integral_prod)
  = volume(Q)·∫_Q h.
 Here ∫_Q 1 dy = volume(Q).toReal, and the constant is pulled out of the integral (integral_const, integral_const_mul). If Q = ∅ (δ ≥ 1/2) the same computation gives 0 = 0. ∎

subproblem.title: Shrinking the unit cube to Q_δ while keeping half of an L¹ norm (parent step 4)
subproblem.statement: Let m ∈ ℕ, Q₁ := {y ∈ Euclid (m + 1) : 0 < y_i < 1 for all i}, Q_δ := {y : δ < y_i < 1 − δ for all i}, and let f be integrable on Q₁. Then there is δ with 0 < δ ≤ 1/4, volume(Q_δ) ≤ 1, volume(Q₁ ∖ Q_δ) ≤ 1/4 and ∫_{Q₁}|f| ≤ 2∫_{Q_δ}|f|.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (m : ℕ) (f : Euclid (m + 1) → ℝ), IntegrableOn f {y : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1} → ∃ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ ∧ δ ≤ 1 / 4 ∧ volume {y : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, δ < y i ∧ y i < 1 - δ} ≤ 1 ∧ volume ({y : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1} \ {y : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, δ < y i ∧ y i < 1 - δ}) ≤ 1 / 4 ∧ ∫ y in {y : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1}, |f y| ≤ 2 * ∫ y in {y : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, δ < y i ∧ y i < 1 - δ}, |f y|
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, step 4 (as in Simon's printed proof of Ch. 2, 2.7: 'choose convex W ⊂⊂ U such that ∫_U|u − β| ≤ 2∫_W|u − β| … for example W = {x ∈ U : dist(x, ∂U) > δ}'). We must choose δ ∈ (0, 1/4] with Lⁿ(Q₁ ∖ Q_δ) ≤ 1/4 and ∫_{Q₁∖Q_δ}|f| ≤ ½∫_{Q₁}|f|, using continuity of measure and of the integral. With Q_δ ⊆ Q₁ the latter is equivalent to ∫_{Q₁}|f| ≤ 2∫_{Q_δ}|f|. In the parent this is applied to f = u − β. Notation: L := volume on Euclid (m + 1).

1. Basic facts.
 – Q₁ and every Q_δ are open (finite intersections of open coordinate half-spaces), hence measurable.
 – L(Q₁) = 1: the coordinate map WithLp.ofLp is measure preserving (PiLp.volume_preserving_ofLp) and maps Q₁ onto the box ∏(0, 1), of measure 1 (Real.volume_pi_Ioo).
 – For δ ≥ 0, Q_δ ⊆ Q₁, hence L(Q_δ) ≤ 1.

2. Exhaustion. Put δ_j := 1/(j + 4) for j ∈ ℕ, so 0 < δ_j ≤ 1/4 and δ_j decreases to 0.
 – The sets Q_{δ_j} increase with j.
 – ⋃_j Q_{δ_j} = Q₁. If y ∈ Q₁ then r := min_i min(y_i, 1 − y_i) > 0 (finitely many coordinates), and y ∈ Q_{δ_j} as soon as δ_j < r.

3. Measure of the boundary layer. The sets Q₁ ∖ Q_{δ_j} are measurable and decreasing, have empty intersection (step 2), and have finite measure (≤ 1). By continuity from above (tendsto_measure_iInter_atTop), L(Q₁ ∖ Q_{δ_j}) → 0. Choose j₁ with L(Q₁ ∖ Q_{δ_j}) ≤ 1/4 for all j ≥ j₁ (the sequence is nonincreasing).

4. Integral. |f| is integrable on Q₁ = ⋃_j Q_{δ_j}, an increasing union of measurable sets. So ∫_{Q_{δ_j}}|f| → ∫_{Q₁}|f| (tendsto_setIntegral_of_monotone).
 – If ∫_{Q₁}|f| = 0, every δ satisfies ∫_{Q₁}|f| = 0 ≤ 2∫_{Q_δ}|f|; put j₂ := 0.
 – Otherwise ∫_{Q₁}|f| > ½∫_{Q₁}|f|, so there is j₂ with ∫_{Q_{δ_j}}|f| ≥ ½∫_{Q₁}|f| for all j ≥ j₂ (the sequence is nondecreasing).

5. Take j := max(j₁, j₂) and δ := δ_j. Then 0 < δ ≤ 1/4, L(Q_δ) ≤ 1 (step 1), L(Q₁ ∖ Q_δ) ≤ 1/4 (step 3) and ∫_{Q₁}|f| ≤ 2∫_{Q_δ}|f| (step 4). ∎

Q_{1/(j+4)} increases to Q₁.
Continuity from above: volume(Q₁ ∖ Q_{1/(j+4)}) → 0.
Continuity of the integral: ∫_{Q_{1/(j+4)}}|f| → ∫_{Q₁}|f|; pick j large for both.

subproblem.title: Fubini identity along the k-th coordinate of the cube Q_δ (parent step 3)
subproblem.statement: Let m ∈ ℕ, δ ∈ ℝ, k ∈ Fin (m + 1), Q_δ := {y ∈ Euclid (m + 1) : δ < y_i < 1 − δ for all i}, and let h : Euclid (m + 1) → ℝ be integrable on Q_δ. For x ∈ Euclid (m + 1) and t ∈ ℝ let x[k ↦ t] be x with its k-th coordinate replaced by t. Then ∫_{Q_δ} ∫_{(δ, 1 − δ)} h(x[k ↦ t]) dt dx = (1 − 2δ)·∫_{Q_δ} h.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (m : ℕ) (δ : ℝ) (k : Fin (m + 1)) (h : Euclid (m + 1) → ℝ), IntegrableOn h {y : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, δ < y i ∧ y i < 1 - δ} → ∫ x in {y : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, δ < y i ∧ y i < 1 - δ}, ∫ t in Ioo δ (1 - δ), h (WithLp.toLp 2 (Function.update (WithLp.ofLp x) k t)) = (1 - 2 * δ) * ∫ x in {y : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, δ < y i ∧ y i < 1 - δ}, h x
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, step 3. The i-th term there is bounded by integrating |∂_i v| along the i-th coordinate segment, and then 'integrating over x, y ∈ Q (Fubini)'. This child is the Fubini identity for integrating along the k-th coordinate: the k-th coordinate of x is a dummy variable, and t takes its place. Notation: E := Euclid (m + 1), μ := volume on E, Q := Q_δ, I := (δ, 1 − δ), x[k ↦ t] := WithLp.toLp 2 (Function.update (WithLp.ofLp x) k t).

0. Degenerate case. If δ ≥ 1/2, no real number lies in I, so Q = ∅ and both sides are 0. Assume δ < 1/2. Then volume(I) = 1 − 2δ > 0 (Real.volume_Ioo).

1. The slice swap ρ. Define ρ : E × ℝ → E × ℝ by ρ(x, t) := (x[k ↦ t], x_k). Then ρ(ρ(x, t)) = (x[k ↦ t][k ↦ x_k], t) = (x, t). So ρ is its own inverse, a measurable equivalence and in particular a measurable embedding.

2. ρ preserves μ ⊗ L¹.
 – Via WithLp.ofLp/toLp (PiLp.volume_preserving_ofLp/toLp, MeasurePreserving.prod with the identity on ℝ), it suffices to show that ρ₀(x, t) := (Function.update x k t, x_k) preserves volume ⊗ volume on ℝ^{Fin (m+1)} × ℝ.
 – The splitting x ↦ (x_k, (x_{k.succAbove j})_{j ∈ Fin m}) is a measure-preserving equivalence ℝ^{Fin (m+1)} ≃ ℝ × ℝ^{Fin m} (MeasurableEquiv.piFinSuccAbove, volume_preserving_piFinSuccAbove). In these coordinates ρ₀ becomes ((a, b), c) ↦ ((c, b), a) on (ℝ × ℝ^{Fin m}) × ℝ.
 – This map is a composition of factor swaps and reassociations: ((a,b),c) ↦ ((b,a),c) ↦ (b,(a,c)) ↦ (b,(c,a)) ↦ ((b,c),a) ↦ ((c,b),a). Each step preserves the product Lebesgue measure (Measure.measurePreserving_swap, measurePreserving_prodAssoc and its inverse, MeasurePreserving.prod). Hence ρ₀, and so ρ, is measure preserving.

3. ρ⁻¹(Q × I) = Q × I. ρ exchanges the k-th coordinate of x with t, and both must lie in I for membership in Q × I. Hence ρ preserves (μ ⊗ L¹)⌞(Q × I) = (μ⌞Q) ⊗ (L¹⌞I) (MeasurePreserving.restrict_preimage_emb, Measure.prod_restrict).

4. Integrability. L¹⌞I is finite. So (x, t) ↦ h(x) is integrable for (μ⌞Q) ⊗ (L¹⌞I) (Integrable.comp_fst). By step 3, so is (x, t) ↦ h(ρ(x, t)₁) = h(x[k ↦ t]) (MeasurePreserving.integrable_comp_emb).

5. Computation.
 ∫_Q ∫_I h(x[k ↦ t]) dt dx
  = ∫_{Q×I} h(ρ(x, t)₁) (Fubini, integral_prod)
  = ∫_{Q×I} h(x) (MeasurePreserving.integral_comp, step 3)
  = ∫_Q volume(I).toReal·h(x) dx (Fubini, integral_const)
  = (1 − 2δ)·∫_Q h (ENNReal.toReal_ofReal, 1 − 2δ ≥ 0). ∎

For x, y let a_k(x, y) have coordinates y_j (j < k), x_j (j ≥ k) and b_k(x, y) have coordinates y_j (j ≤ k), x_j (j > k), and let e_k := EuclideanSpace.single k 1. Source: parent proof, step 3. There, v(x) − v(y) = Σ_i [v(w^{i−1}) − v(w^i)], each difference is bounded by '∫ over the segment between x_i and y_i of |∂_i v|', and 'integrating over x, y ∈ Q (Fubini) bounds the i-th term by s·Lⁿ(Q)·∫_Q|∂_i v|'. This child is that bound for one index. In 0-based indexing, a_k = w^k and b_k = w^{k+1}.
Dependencies: sibling mixed_point_identity (Submission.dor_lmb_fcd_cp_mixed_point_integral) and sibling slice_identity (Submission.dor_lmb_fcd_cp_slice_integral).
Notation: E := Euclid (m + 1), Q := Q_δ, I := (δ, 1 − δ), s := 1 − 2δ > 0, ∂_k v(p) := Dv(p)e_k. For p ∈ E and t ∈ ℝ, p[t] := WithLp.toLp 2 (Function.update (WithLp.ofLp p) k t), the point p with k-th coordinate t; note p[t] = p + (t − p_k)e_k. Put Φ(p) := ∫_I |∂_k v(p[t])| dt.

1. Pointwise bound via the fundamental theorem of calculus. Let x, y ∈ Q, a := a_k(x, y), b := b_k(x, y).

subproblem.title: Total variation of a smooth function on a bounded open set by duality with test fields (parent step 5)
subproblem.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, W ⊆ Euclid P open and bounded, w : Euclid P → ℝ of class C^∞ and V ∈ ℝ. Assume ∫ Dw(y)(g(y)) dy ≤ V for every C^∞ map g : Euclid P → Euclid P with compact support, tsupport g ⊆ W and |g(y)| ≤ 1 for all y. Then ∫_W ‖Dw(y)‖ dy ≤ V.

Source: parent proof, step 5: '|Du_ε| is continuous, so ∫_W|Du_ε| is the supremum of ∫_W Du_ε·g over C^∞ compactly supported g with |g| ≤ 1, by approximating Du_ε/|Du_ε| truncated'. This child proves the needed inequality ∫_W‖Dw‖ ≤ sup_g ∫ Dw·g for a C^∞ function w.
Dependency: sibling smooth_cutoff (Submission.rsd_mw_tfa_smooth_cutoff).
Notation: E := Euclid P, L := volume, e_i := EuclideanSpace.single i 1.

1. V ≥ 0. The field g ≡ 0 is admissible (C^∞, empty support, |0| ≤ 1) and gives ∫ Dw(y)(0) dy = 0 ≤ V.

2. Gradient field. Let F(y) := WithLp.toLp 2 (i ↦ Dw(y)e_i) ∈ E.
 – Writing h = Σ_i h_i e_i: ⟨F(y), h⟩ = Σ_i h_i·Dw(y)e_i = Dw(y)h for all h.
 – Hence InnerProductSpace.toDual ℝ E (F(y)) = Dw(y), and since the Riesz map is an isometry, |F(y)| = ‖Dw(y)‖.
 – F is C^∞. w is C^∞, so y ↦ Dw(y) is C^∞ (ContDiff.fderiv_right). Each component y ↦ Dw(y)e_i is C^∞ (ContDiff.clm_apply). The coordinate equivalence (WithLp.linearEquiv 2 ℝ (Fin P → ℝ)).symm is continuous linear (contDiff_pi).

3. Bounds. W is bounded, so its closure W̄ is compact (finite dimension) and L(W) < ∞. F is continuous, so M := sup_{W̄}|F| < ∞; take M ≥ 0. All functions below are measurable and bounded on W, hence integrable on W.

4. Cut-offs. Fix j ∈ ℕ and put ε := 1/(j + 1). Apply the sibling smooth_cutoff with ν := L⌞W, V := W and δ := ε. This is legitimate: ν is finite because L(W) < ∞; W is open; ν(Wᶜ) = L(Wᶜ ∩ W) = 0. We get a C^∞ function χ with compact support, tsupport χ ⊆ W, 0 ≤ χ ≤ 1 and L(W ∩ {χ ≠ 1}) = ν{χ ≠ 1} < ε.

5. Test field. Let g(y) := χ(y)·F(y)/√(|F(y)|² + ε²).
 – g is C^∞: |F|² = ⟨F, F⟩ is C^∞ (ContDiff.inner); |F|² + ε² ≥ ε² > 0, so its square root is C^∞ (ContDiff.sqrt) and nonvanishing; products and quotients by nonvanishing C^∞ functions are C^∞.
 – support g ⊆ support χ, so g has compact support and tsupport g ⊆ tsupport χ ⊆ W.
 – |g| ≤ χ·|F|/√(|F|² + ε²) ≤ 1.
 So g is admissible, and by hypothesis ∫ Dw(y)(g(y)) dy ≤ V. Moreover Dw(y)(g(y)) = ⟨F(y), g(y)⟩ = ψ(y), where ψ := χ·|F|²/√(|F|² + ε²) ≥ 0, and ψ vanishes outside W. Hence ∫_W ψ ≤ V.

6. Estimate. For y ∈ W,
 |F| − ψ = (1 − χ)·|F|²/√(|F|² + ε²) + (|F| − |F|²/√(|F|² + ε²)).
 – The first term is ≤ M·1_{χ ≠ 1}: it is 0 where χ = 1, and |F|²/√(|F|² + ε²) ≤ |F| ≤ M with 0 ≤ 1 − χ ≤ 1.
 – The second term is ≤ ε: for a ≥ 0, a − a²/√(a² + ε²) = a(√(a² + ε²) − a)/√(a² + ε²) ≤ √(a² + ε²) − a ≤ ε.
 Integrating over W ({χ ≠ 1} is open, hence measurable):
 ∫_W|F| ≤ ∫_W ψ + M·L(W ∩ {χ ≠ 1}) + ε·L(W) ≤ V + (M + L(W))/(j + 1).

7. Letting j → ∞ gives ∫_W ‖Dw(y)‖ dy = ∫_W |F| ≤ V. ∎

Here W = Q_δ, and the support condition on η replaces ε < δ.
Dependencies: sibling smooth_duality (Submission.dor_lmb_fcd_cp_smooth_duality) and sibling mollifier_adjoint (Submission.codim1_rdo_dg_sp_mollifier_adjoint).

Source: parent proof, step 3 (smooth Poincaré inequality on cubes, by coordinate paths): for a cube Q of side s = 1 − 2δ, ∫_Q∫_Q|v(x) − v(y)| ≤ Σ_i s·Lⁿ(Q)·∫_Q|∂_i v| ≤ n·s·Lⁿ(Q)·∫_Q|Dv|, with n = m + 1.
Dependency: sibling coordinate_step (Submission.dor_lmb_fcd_cp_coordinate_step).
Notation: E := Euclid (m + 1), Q := Q_δ, e_k := EuclideanSpace.single k 1. For k ∈ Fin (m + 1), a_k and b_k are as in coordinate_step.

1. Telescoping (coordinate paths). For x, y ∈ E and r ∈ {0, …, m + 1}, let W_r(x, y) := WithLp.toLp 2 (j ↦ y_j if (j : ℕ) < r else x_j).
 – W_0 = x, because no j has j < 0.
 – W_{m+1} = y, because every j ∈ Fin (m + 1) has j < m + 1.
 – For k ∈ Fin (m + 1): W_k = a_k(x, y), since (j : ℕ) < (k : ℕ) ⟺ j < k. Also W_{k+1} = b_k(x, y), since (j : ℕ) < k + 1 ⟺ j ≤ k.
 Hence (Finset.sum_range_sub' after Fin.sum_univ_eq_sum_range)
 v(x) − v(y) = Σ_{r=0}^{m} (v(W_r) − v(W_{r+1})) = Σ_{k ∈ Fin (m+1)} (v(a_k(x, y)) − v(b_k(x, y))),
 and so |v(x) − v(y)| ≤ Σ_k |v(a_k(x, y)) − v(b_k(x, y))|.

2. Integrability. v is continuous and Q̄ is compact; for x, y ∈ Q every W_r(x, y) lies in Q. So all functions (x, y) ↦ |v(x) − v(y)| and (x, y) ↦ |v(a_k) − v(b_k)| are continuous and bounded on Q × Q. Since volume(Q) < ∞ (Q is bounded), they are integrable for (volume⌞Q) ⊗ (volume⌞Q). Their partial integrals in y are integrable in x (Fubini). Hence the iterated integrals are monotone and additive over the finite sum (integral_finset_sum, applied to the inner and then to the outer integral).

Here the passage to the limit is made directly in that double integral, for the mollifications along a sequence, and only almost-everywhere convergence (Lebesgue's differentiation theorem, supplied as a hypothesis) is used together with Fatou's lemma. This yields the same limit inequality as the parent's L¹-convergence argument; the mean form ∫_W|u − ū| ≤ n·s·V of the parent follows from it by the Jensen step of the sibling median_deviation.
